core_obligations: Form the product and the graph (proof lines 6611-6612): set M = U x_X U' and let Gamma_h be the graph of h, a subscheme of the closed fibre M_Z.

Show the graph is open (proof lines 6612-6614): Gamma_h is the image of a section of the etale morphism pr_{1,Z} : M_Z -> U_Z, and the image of a section of an etale morphism is open, so Gamma_h is open in M_Z.

Lift to an open subscheme of the product (proof lines 6615-6617): choose an open subscheme W of M whose intersection with M_Z is Gamma_h, and set a = pr_1|_W and b = pr_2|_W, which gives the required diagram with a_Z an isomorphism and h = b_Z composed with its inverse.
proof_roadmap: Take the fibre product of the two etale X-schemes and the graph of the given morphism in its closed fibre.
Identify the graph with the image of a section of an etale morphism, hence an open subscheme.
Lift that open subscheme to an open subscheme of the product.
Its two projections realise h as a composite of an isomorphism and a morphism in X_etale, up to the closed immersion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma realises a morphism h between the closed fibres of two etale X-schemes by a correspondence in X_etale, that is, by an object W with morphisms a : W -> U and b : W -> U' such that a_Z is an isomorphism and h = b_Z composed with a_Z^{-1} (statement lines 6596-6608). The proof identifies the graph Gamma_h inside the closed fibre of M = U x_X U' with the image of a section of the etale morphism pr_{1,Z}, so that openness of such images makes Gamma_h open, and then lifts that open piece to an open subscheme W of M (proof lines 6611-6617). The non-formal content is exactly the recognition of the graph as a section image, which is what makes the lift possible. The claim is H2: one geometric construction with a single non-formal identification.
